observation.visible_scene: An outdoor concrete patio with a vertical expansion seam, a brick-paved edge on the right, and two thin black tripod legs at the top. On the left a person's pale trouser leg and dark sneaker stand still. A Spalding/NBA basketball hangs in mid-air near the center, and a hand enters from the top edge of the frame.
visible_changes: The basketball moves upward within the frame and grows slightly larger (closer to the lens), drifting a little to the right; its surface markings (SPALDING / NBA text and the curved seams) rotate gradually as it rises.

The hand descends from the top edge toward the ball. Early on it is blurred with only two extended fingers (a pointing/V shape); as it lowers it comes into sharper focus, the palm rotates and the fingers splay open.
The gap between hand and ball closes steadily: by the later frames the spread fingers overlap the upper surface of the ball, appearing to rest on or reach for its top.
The background (pavement, seam, brick edge, tripod legs, leg and shoe) stays in fixed positions, indicating the apparent motion is from the ball and hand rather than camera movement.
outside_clip_unknowns: What set the ball in motion before this segment (a throw, a bounce, or a release) is not shown.
Whether the hand actually grips, deflects, or merely hovers over the ball, and what happens after the last frame, is not visible.
uncertain_details: The ball's upward travel and enlargement could be true motion toward/away from the camera or partly a perspective effect; the exact 3D trajectory is uncertain.
Whether finger-to-ball contact is established at the end is ambiguous due to blur and overlap.
The hand's initial two-finger appearance may be partial occlusion at the frame edge rather than a fixed gesture.
